newsitem.title: USA: LatAm Brady debt hurt by more Brazil bribe charges.
newsitem.headline: LatAm Brady debt hurt by more Brazil bribe charges.

text.p: Most Latin American Brady bonds gave ground in light trading Wednesday amid further allegations of bribery in the Brazil government, traders said.
Spreads in the region widened about five basis points on average, led by a 10-basis-point widening in Brazil.
"There have been some big trades in Brazil, but there has been very little activity from customers," one trader said.
Brazil Bradys again declined after the bribery allegations reported in a local newspaper Tuesday were linked by the newspaper to a leading Cabinet minister on Wednesday.
In late trading, Brazil "C" bonds were off 1/4 at 75-3/4.

The daily Folha de Sao Paolo said it had taped conversations implicating Communications Minister Sergio Motta in a vote-buying scandal. Folha alleged Motta knew funds were paid to state leaders in order to secure votes for an amendment allowing certain officials to run for reelection.
Market experts in New York were reluctant to take a bearish longer term view on Brazil, noting that the allegations had not yet been investigated.
"My personal opinion is that Motta is not going to resign and he will say that all of what they have is nonsense," another trader said. "We'll take a good tone after that."
The trader said Brazil debt had lagged in the recent rally and may present a better buying opportunity now.
"You have C bonds trading now at 500 (basis points) over when Argentina '17s are trading at 380 over, and C bonds have a much shorter duration," he said.
Brazil analysts interviewed earlier in the day said their outlook on the country remained neutral to slightly negative.
Argentina FRBs slipped 1/8 to 92-1/4 bid and Mexico Discounts fell 1/4 to 90 bid.
"Argentina is just following Brazil on the downturn, but not as much," a trader said.

Mexico's finance ministry on Wednesday said it will use the proceeds of its five-year, 300 million sterling Eurobond to refinance short-term debt. One Brady trader said the country was rumored to be mulling a buyback of some Bradys, but other market sources said they doubted that was the case.
More broadly, Bulgaria FLRBs were off 3/8 at 50-3/4, dollar-denominated Vnesh were unchanged at 83-3/4 and Russian MinFins ranged between off 1/2 and up 1/2.
